doc.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017

title: Scales as the foundation of jazz chords
summary: Mullins and Rowe agree chords are built on scales, unlike classical music's melody line.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I was glad to hear you say about the scales though, because I tell my sax players, “If you can’t play your scales, how are you going to look at a chord symbol and figure out what it is?”
That’s right. The scales are the background of the chords. You know, the chords are built on the scale.
If you’re familiar with your scales, it’s not that hard. It’s not exactly easy at first because you have, in classical music you don’t deal with the chords. It’s melody line.
